'''Nancy Blachman''' (born 1956 in [[Palo Alto, California|Palo Alto, CA]]) is an American educator, supporter of [[recreational mathematics]] and mathematical [[outreach]], software book author, and supporter of [[Independent film|indie]] [[Documentary film|documentary]] films.<ref name=IMDB>[https://www.imdb.com/name/nm6011483/?ref%20=ttfc%20fc%20cr2 Nancy Blachman] at IMDB</ref> In 2007, she founded the [[Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival]] (JRMF),<ref name=fest>[https://www.msri.org/web/msri/education/for-k-12-educators/julia-robinson-math-festival Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival] [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]]</ref> which has grown into a successful math enrichment enterprise for teenagers in the USA and beyond.  She is a long time supporter of the educational foundation [[Gathering 4 Gardner]].<ref name=g4g>[https://www.gathering4gardner.org/board-of-directors/ Board Of Directors] Gathering 4 Gardner</ref> She is a former chair and remains on the advisory board of Berkeley’s Industrial Engineering and Operations Research Department (IEOR).<ref>[https://ieor.berkeley.edu/advisory-board/ Advisory Board] Berkeley Industrial Engineering and Operations Research Department</ref>

==Early life and education==
Nancy Blachman was born in 1956 in Palo Alto, California, her father Nelson being an electrical engineer.<ref>[http://www.blachman.org/ The Blachman Family Home Page]</ref><ref>[http://www.blachman.org/nelson/ Nelson M. Blachman] CV</ref> The family spent some time living in Spain in the 1960s, and Nancy's interest in mathematics began during high school back in [[Palo Alto, California|Palo Alto]] when she took a course based on [[George Pólya|George Polya]]'s
''[[Mathematics and Plausible Reasoning]]''.<ref name=berkeley/> She was also inspired by the mathematics contest produced by [[Saint Mary's College of California]]<ref name=marycontest>[https://www.amazon.com/College-Mathematics-Contest-Problems-Junior/dp/B01LBHKVLS Saint Mary's College Mathematics Contest Problems For Junior and Senior High School]</ref> then popular with secondary schools throughout the San Francisco Bay Area.<ref name=SMMC>[http://www.gathering4gardner.org/g4g12gift/Blachman_Nancy-Saint_Marys_Math.pdf Saint Mary’s Math Contest: High School Division] : by Nancy Blachman & Nick Baxter</ref>

She did undergraduate work at [[University of California, San Diego]] (1974 to 1976), got honours B.Sc. in [[applied mathematics]] from the [[University of Birmingham]] in the [[United Kingdom|UK]] (1978), an M.S. in [[operations research]] from [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1979) and an M.S. in [[computer science]] at [[Stanford University]] (1988).<ref name=berkeley>[https://ieor.berkeley.edu/advisory%20board/nancy-blachman/ Nancy Blachman] Berkeley Industrial Engineering and Operations Research Department</ref><ref>[http://www.variablesymbols.com/resume.html Blachman resume] Variable Symbols</ref>

==Mathematics in education==
Blachman taught a course in problem solving with [[Mathematica]] at Stanford from 1990 to 1997.<ref name=inform>[https://www.informit.com/authors/bio/61dc8e26-2ea9-4f3d-9d59-705b704ea208 Authors: Nancy Blachman] [[InformIT]]</ref>

In 2004 she created Google Guide, an online interactive tutorial and reference about the capabilities of [[Google]].<ref>''[https://www.googleguide.com/ Google Guide: An Interactive Tutorial on Searching with Google]'', by Nancy Blachman, GoogleGuide.com, OCLC Number: 53451437</ref>

In 2005 while attending an education forum that promoted [[STEM]] [Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math]<ref name=JewishNews>[https://jweekly.com/2022/08/04/qa-how-do-you-get-kids-to-love-math-try-a-festival/ How do you get kids to love math? Try a festival. The Jewish News of Northern California]</ref> she remembered how the Saint Mary's College Mathematics Contest had inspired her as a student.<ref name=SMMC/><ref>[https://www.siliconvalleycf.org/about/news-media/blog/nancy-blachman-uses-donor-advised-fund-inspire-students-love-math Silicon Valley Community Foundation]</ref> Working with Joshua Zucker and Jim Sotiros she decided to revive the structure and spirit of this long defunct competition.<ref name=jrmf>[https://www.jrmf.org/history/ History of JRMF] By Nancy Blachman, JRMF Founder</ref> This led to the founding of the Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival in 2007.<ref name=fest/>  JRMF events now occur throughout the United States and have reached more than 100,000 students worldwide.<ref>[https://jrmf.org/blog/jrmf-founder-nancy-blachman-featured-by-uc-berkeley/ Julia Robinson Mathematics Festival Founder Nancy Blachman Featured By UC Berkeley]</ref>

Blachman has been a board member of Gathering 4 Gardner since 2008, served as its chair from 2012 to 2020, and is currently board president.<ref name=g4g/>

She is the president and founder of Variable Symbols, a company that provides training, books, and tools to make complex software easier to use.<ref name=variable>[http://www.variablesymbols.com/index.html Nancy Blachman] Variable Symbols, Inc.</ref>

==Indie documentary films==
Blachman has been working since 2015 with filmmakers to shine a light on people in difficult situations, to uplift marginalized voices, humanize them, and make their stories accessible—with the aim of encouraging viewers to take action.  Documentaries she has supported include ''Aftershock, Art Spiegelman: Disaster is My Muse, Ailey, Athlete A, Counted Out, Crip Camp, Dark Money, Free for All, Patrice: The Movie, The Fight'', and ''The Social Dilemma''.<ref>[https://eddysworld.net/team/  Nancy Blachman] ''Eddy's World'' (documentary)</ref>

==Personal life==
On January 1, 1999, she married David desJardins. They have two children, Sarah and Louis.<ref name=bio>[http://www.variablesymbols.com/bio.html Nancy Blachman Biography]</ref>
